chapter: Bands and bandleading in New Orleans
title: Playing with Val Barbera and the Joe's Inn band
summary: After sitting in with Barbera, Bergen recalls clubs of 1937 and then a Jefferson Highway job at Joe's Inn with several local players, up to about 1939.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Okay, Bergen we've got the third reel on.

In fact, Val was so used to using good musicians that one time I sat in with him and he heard a bad note and he kind of got on to me. So you can see the guy can always give you a good band. And it amazed me. I thought he didn't hear that note because I tried to bring it in with a chord to make it blend. Anyway I played with Barbera quite a while. And then after that, around 1937, some of the clubs we played in, Dick, was the old little club that used to be on Brown Street. And of course they rented it off of dancers. That thing was heavily draped all the way around with velvet and boy, the bigger the band the better it sounded. There was another place where the acoustics were very good, never did it sound too loud. And I'm trying to think after I left Frank, Barbera would have my daddy died if I let down. In the 40s? Yeah. I started drifting in little joints up on the airline highway, or Jefferson Highway. I think it was Vernon Roccaford had a job at a place called Joe's Inn, who was right across from the first O'Shaughnessy filling station, got a corner at the Tunkin Steakhouse. Joe Piccararo, he ran it. And I believe he ended up marrying Abby Brunas' first wife if I ain't mistaken. I believe his wife was Abby's wife at one time. And we had a good little band in there. We played a lot of the jazz tunes, and of course popular tunes too. And Joe Hellick played pretty good sax. We had Morris Escario piano. Big Bill Craig used to play. Not Bill Craigs but Bill Craig. And I had a bass player from out of town, but we had a pretty good band. I enjoyed playing there. And of course that band would break up and I'd go back there with another band. One time it was Steve Massico, Jeff Riddick, and Speck Reagan I believe, and myself. And that was about 1939. I can remember it very distinctly. And after 1939 I was – what happened about that time? Joe was in. Let's see.
